title: Algebraic World Model Induces Category-Theoretic Rules and Proves Impossibility in Lean 4
aiSystem: Algebraic World Model (AWM) + Claude Opus 5 + Lean 4
whyItMatters: Bridges empirical exploration and formal mathematics: autonomously discovers unknown environment laws, formalizes them in Lean 4, and outputs kernel-checked impossibility proofs where frontier LLMs score 0/12.
summary: Researchers at Tsinghua University IIIS led by Andrew Chi-Chih Yao and Yang Yuan introduced the Algebraic World Model (AWM), a neuro-symbolic agent (paired with Claude Opus 5) that actively probes unknown environments, abstracts their transition dynamics into typed category-theoretic algebraic structures, and compiles those models into Lean 4. Beyond clearing all 183 levels across all 25 public ARC-AGI-3 interactive environments (99.9 score using 43% of human baseline actions), AWM autonomously constructs closed, kernel-checked Lean 4 impossibility proofs demonstrating that no legal action sequence can reach a goal on unsolvable levels (6/6 runs vs. 0/12 for Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra).
technicalHighlights: Induces formal category-theoretic algebraic specifications directly from black-box environment interactions and verifies them in the Lean 4 kernel.
Autonomously constructs closed Lean 4 impossibility proofs excluding all legal winning sequences on unsolvable levels (6/6 runs vs. 0/12 for frontier LLM baselines).
Clears all 183 levels across all 25 public ARC-AGI-3 interactive games with a 99.9 score at 43% of human baseline actions.
caveats: Lean kernel verification guarantees the impossibility proofs hold for the induced formal model, while faithfulness of the induced model to the underlying environment relies on active empirical testing; manuscript is an October 2026 preprint.

scoreRationale.foundational: Demonstrates end-to-end transition from black-box empirical exploration to kernel-checked formal impossibility theorems.
scoreRationale.ripple: Connects category-theoretic world modeling with formal verification for robotics, software safety, and autonomous science.
scoreRationale.verification: Impossibility proofs are machine-checked by the Lean 4 kernel with zero sorry placeholders, alongside full empirical evaluation.
scoreRationale.velocity: Autonomously synthesizes rules, plans, and formal proofs without human-authored formal specifications.

sources.label: Pan, Tan, Yuan & Yao — Algebraic World Model: From Exploration to Proofs (arXiv:2610.40503)
